## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search (e.g., BM25) with dense vector search to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity. The two ranked result sets are merged, typically via reciprocal rank fusion, to produce a unified ranking.

This pattern excels on queries that mix:
- Rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs) — better handled by sparse lexical search
- Natural language intent — better captured by dense semantic search

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone on such mixed-mode queries and has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems.

### Reciprocal Rank Fusion

Reciprocal rank fusion is a common merging strategy for combining multiple ranked result sets. It provides a principled way to integrate results from both sparse and dense retrievers into a single ranked list.
